newsitem.title: USA: US fund sponsors prefer active FX management - poll.
newsitem.headline: US fund sponsors prefer active FX management - poll.

text.p: U.S. pension funds, endowments and foundations are more likely to use active rather than passive currency management in pursing their international investment objectives, according to a survey released Tuesday by Goldman, Sachs and Co and Rogers, Casey and Associates Inc.

"Despite this widespread preference for active currency management, pension funds display virtually no enthusiasm for investing in currencies as a separate and distinct asset class," said Thomas Healey, a Goldman Sachs' partner and head of the firm's Pension Services Group.
The plan sponsor currency survey polled 66 major corporate, public and foundation funds with a median asset size of $6.4 billion. Funds with no international assets were excluded from the survey.

Value-added potential and risk reduction were the primary reasons why the majority of funds choose active currency management for both international equity and fixed-income portfolios, the survey said.
The vast majority of funds have their currency exposure managed externally, according to the poll.

A third of funds surveyed use specialist external managers for the currency exposure of their equity allocations, but far fewer hire specialists to manage currency exposure of their fixed-income portfolios, the survey showed.
Survey data seem to reflect acceptance of the proposition that hedging policy should change as plan allocations to international assets grow past 20 percent, it said.
In fact, plan sponsors cited allocation level to international investments as the most critical factor in setting currency hedging policy, the survey showed.

While there was no significant difference between large and small funds in their average allocation to international assets, only the smaller funds expressed an appetite for additional exposure, according to the poll.

Corporate plan respondents had a higher allocation to international assets than did public funds, with the median corporate respondent allocating 19 percent and the median public fund participant allocating 13 percent, it said.
The majority of funds have unhedged equity and fixed-income benchmarks as the policy for managing their currency exposure, the survey said.
